svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.15.4.2 Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.15 FOOTINGS AND FOUNDATIONS
Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support

g.text: at the top by the floor
Flat ICF core: not less than
the greater of 150 mm or the
Maximum height of finished ground above basement
floor or crawl space ground cover, m
Solid concrete and concrete core in flat wall ICF (3), 15 MPa min. strength
Solid concrete and concrete core in flat wall ICF (3), 20 MPa min. strength
Size and spacing of continuous vertical reinforcement, M at mm o.c.
H = maximum height of finished ground above basement floor or crawl space ground cover.
(1) See Article 9.15.4.3. (2) See Article 9.15.4.6. (3) No reinforcement required.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Foundation walls of unreinforced concrete block, flat ICF
concrete core or solid concrete subject to lateral earth
pressure: thickness to Table 9.15.4.2.-A, for walls not more
than 3.0 m (9′-10⅛″) in unsupported height
The concrete core of flat ICF foundation walls is not less
than the greater of 150 mm (5⅞″) or the thickness of the
concrete in the wall above
Reinforced concrete block walls conform to Table 9.15.4.2.-B
and Sentences (4) to (7) where the walls are laterally
supported at the top, average stable soils are encountered
and wind loads on the exposed foundation are no greater than
Continuous vertical bars at corners, ends, intersections,
changes in wall height, jambs of all openings and movement
joints, from the top of the footing to the top of the wall
Where the wall is laterally supported at the top and the floor
slab does not provide lateral support at the base, embedded not
less than 50 mm (1 15/16″) into the footing.
A continuous bond beam with not less than one 15M bar along
the top, at the sill and head of openings over 1.20 m
(3′-11¼″) wide, and at structurally connected floors
All vertical bars on the centre line of the wall
Ladder- or truss-type lateral reinforcement not less than
3.8 mm in diameter (no. 9 ASWG) in the bed joint of every
second course
Drawn: A cut through a concrete wall, B cut through a grouted, reinforced core. Sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.15.4.2. (page 9-121), tables on pages 9-122 to 9-124, with Note A-Table 9.15.4.2.-A
